tools.attach_description: Attach a file from the sandbox directly to the task (a PDF you generated, a report, a build artifact). The bytes are read out of the sandbox server-side and stored full-fidelity — NEVER base64-encode a file yourself and paste it into a tool call: that path downscales/corrupts binaries. This is the way to deliver any binary evidence that isn't a browser screenshot (for those, use thulu-browser's screenshot with task_id). Max 50MB.
tools.attach_filename: Label shown in the dashboard. Defaults to the file's basename.
tools.attach_mime_type: MIME type. Inferred from the filename extension when omitted (e.g. application/pdf).
tools.attach_path: Absolute path to the file inside the sandbox (e.g. /tmp/out/report.pdf).
tools.attach_unavailable: attach_file is unavailable: no attachment sink is wired on this server
tools.exec_description: Run a shell command inside the task's sandbox container. Each call gets a fresh shell (no state survives between calls — `cd` does not persist). Use this for builds, tests, lint runs, or starting dev servers (use `setsid nohup ... &` to detach a long-running process). Output is capped at ~100KB per stream; redirect to a file and read it back if you need the full log.
tools.exec_env: Extra env vars merged on top of the sandbox env.
tools.exec_timeout: Hard kill after this ms. Default 300000 (5min), max 1800000 (30min).
tools.file_empty: file is empty or does not exist: {path}
tools.preview_cluster_note: On Kubernetes the sandbox ports are not published outside the cluster: only this task's pods (your thulu-browser among them) can open this URL, and there is no address for a person. The first request after the sandbox starts can be refused for a few seconds while the network policy is applied; retry.
tools.preview_description: Return connection info for a port your dev server is listening on inside the sandbox. Returns {url, human_url, port}: `url` is what thulu-browser must open; `human_url` is what to share with a person on the host, and is empty on Kubernetes, where the ports stay inside the cluster (`note` then explains). The dev server must listen on 0.0.0.0, not 127.0.0.1, to be reachable. Exposed ports: {ports}.
tools.preview_port: Port the service listens on inside the sandbox.
tools.queued_message: sandbox capacity full; you have been queued. The dispatcher will relaunch this stage when a slot frees.
tools.queued_retry: queued — sandbox capacity full, retry shortly
tools.init_project_arg: Project name (or its directory under /workspace/projects, or its id). Optional when the task has a single project.
tools.init_status_description: Call it first. For each project of this task: whether Thulu has an init script that brings it up in this sandbox, its revision, params (with defaults), ports, ready command, its install phase (has_setup, tools, cache) and the state of the last run in this sandbox (never|running|ready|failed|timeout) with its phase, what setup did, times and log path. If a project has a script, use init_run instead of installing dependencies or guessing how to start it.
tools.init_run_description: Run the project's stored init script in this sandbox, in two phases, from /workspace/projects/<project>/<workdir>, detached (setsid), with the params as env vars plus OCTOPUS_PROJECT, OCTOPUS_TASK_ID, OCTOPUS_INIT_FILES and, for every port the sandbox publishes, OCTOPUS_PREVIEW_URL_<port> (the url preview_url returns for it; default a front end's API URL param to it instead of hard-coding a sandbox address). First the install phase: tools are installed with mise, then setup is skipped when this checkout already has its output for the same setup key (setup + tools + cache.key files), restored from the default branch's snapshot when one exists, or run. Then the start script (copied to /tmp/octopus-init/<project>/run.sh). A previous run of the same project is stopped first (its whole process group). With wait=true (default) it polls the ready command every 2 s once the start script runs, until it exits 0 or the manifest timeout passes (the install has its own 30 min cap), and returns {state, phase, setup {status skipped|restored|ran|failed, key, timings}, elapsed_ms, ports, log_tail}. Setup output goes to the same log. If it fails because of an incompatibility, fix the script with init_script_update and run it again.
tools.init_run_params: Values for the params the manifest declares, by name. Unknown names are rejected; missing ones take their default; required ones without a default must be given.
tools.init_run_wait: Wait for ready (default true). false returns at once with state running; check later with init_status.
tools.init_get_description: Read the project's current init script: the script, its manifest (params, ports, ready, workdir), revision and who wrote it. Read it before changing it with init_script_update.
tools.init_update_description: Save a new revision of the project's init script (the full script and manifest, not a diff). It applies right away and keeps history; you sign it as this agent run. Use it when the script breaks on an incompatibility (fix it, then init_run again) and when a project has no script and you managed to bring it up: save the steps that worked so the next task starts from them. Manifest: params [{name ^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*$, description, default, required}], ports [int], ready {command (exit 0 = up), timeout_seconds (default 300, max 900)}, workdir (relative to the repo root, default "."), setup (install script: put dependency installs here, not in script), tools {name: version} for mise instead of curl-installing toolchains, cache {key: [lock files], paths: [directories setup fills]}, files {path: text}: helper files the script reads from $OCTOPUS_INIT_FILES; sandbox helpers go there, never into the project's repo. With setup and cache.paths, Thulu snapshots the setup output from the default branch and later tasks restore it instead of installing.
tools.init_update_script: The whole bash script. It runs with bash from the workdir; params arrive as env vars. Start long-running servers in the background (nohup ... &) or run them in the foreground as the last step; both work.
tools.init_update_manifest: How the script is run: params, ports, ready, workdir, and the install phase: setup, tools, cache.
tools.init_update_note: One line on what changed and why, shown in the history (e.g. "pin node 20: pnpm 9 needs it").
tools.init_status_hint: Projects with has_script=true: start them with init_run. Projects without one: bring them up by hand, then save what worked with init_script_update.
tools.init_no_script: Project {project} has no init script yet. Bring it up by hand with exec, then save the steps that worked with init_script_update so the next task can use init_run.
tools.init_not_mounted: Project {project} has no worktree in this sandbox yet, so its script cannot run here.
tools.init_none_yet: Project {project} has no init script yet (revision 0).
tools.init_saved: Saved the init script of {project} as revision {revision}.
tools.init_superseded: a newer init_run of this project replaced this run
tools.init_recovered: read back from the sandbox: the daemon restarted after this run started, so finished_at is unknown
tools.init_tools_failed: Installing the tools with mise failed. Check the versions in manifest.tools (or the repo's mise file) and the log.
tools.init_setup_failed: The setup phase failed (exit {code}); the start script did not run. See the log.
tools.init_update_setup: Install phase: a bash script run from the workdir before the start script (npm ci, go mod download, pip install). It is skipped when the sandbox already has its output for the same lock files, and restored from a snapshot of the default branch when there is one. Put installs here, not in script.
tools.init_update_tools: Toolchains for mise, name to version, e.g. {"go": "1.25.1", "node": "22"}. Setup and the start script run under them. Leave it empty when the repo has mise.toml, .mise.toml or .tool-versions; do not curl-install toolchains in the script.
tools.init_update_cache: key: the lock files whose content decides the setup output (package-lock.json, go.sum). paths: the directories setup fills (node_modules, .venv). Both relative to the workdir. Without paths there are no snapshots.
tools.init_setup_summary_skipped: setup: skipped, already done for key {key}
tools.init_setup_summary_ran_no_cache: setup: ran in {elapsed} (this sandbox has no dependency cache)
tools.init_update_files: Support files the setup and the script use, path → text (a seed script, a static server, a package.json for a helper). They are stored in Thulu with the revision and written to $OCTOPUS_INIT_FILES/<path> in the sandbox before each run, outside the repo. Put sandbox helpers here: never commit them to the project's repo. Up to 32 files, 64 KiB each, 256 KiB in all. Editing one re-runs the setup.

init_setup.no_mise: the manifest declares tools but this image has no mise; continuing without installing them
init_setup.no_cache: this sandbox has no dependency cache (OCTOPUS_CACHE_DIR unset): running setup without looking for a snapshot
init_setup.skipped: setup skipped: this checkout already has the output of key
init_setup.restoring: restoring the setup output from the snapshot of key
init_setup.restore_failed: the snapshot could not be unpacked; running setup instead

setup_log.interrupted: the run ended ({state}) before the install finished
